Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational warranty & cross-border transfer checklist

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — we're getting close to legal signoff on the purchase order but need two things before we proceed: a short operational warranty section in the DPA that clarifies whether Redwood will process customer data outside of the EU/UK for any of the services referenced in the SOW, and a current subprocessor inventory.

Specifically our security team asked: 1) Will telemetry/cache or metadata ever be replicated outside the EU for redundancy? 2) If you rely on third-party CDNs or monitoring tools, can you list the subprocessors and their jurisdictions? 3) Do you have a standard fallback/continuity clause tied to SCCs / UK IDTA?

I've attached the WellBridge DPA template and flagged the clause placeholder. Can you confirm who on your side will own legal and technical answers and an estimated timeline to get redlines back?

Appreciate it — Sandra

Hi Sandra,

Thanks — looping in Kimberly (legal) and Jordan (privacy/ops). We'll review the DPA and provide a redline focusing on the three items you called out. Initial plan:

- Kimberly will propose language for an operational warranty + fallback tied to SCCs/UK IDTA (we generally commit to processing inside contracted regions and fall back to compatible model variants when necessary).
- Jordan will scope whether telemetry/metrics and KV cache are replicated for redundancy and propose any TIA (technical impact assessment) scope needed for caching/telemetry.
- I will coordinate procurement cadence and confirm subprocessors list (we'll provide Annex A updated CSV).

Can you confirm whether WellBridge requires the subprocessor list with contact jurisdiction + whether you expect evidence for HSM/KMS use? That will change the scope of artifacts we need to assemble.

I'll aim to get a legal redline and the Annex A inventory by Monday 2027-11-01 EOD.

Subject: Re: Operational warranty & cross-border transfer checklist

Sandra / Grace — quick read of the DPA attached. Two substantive asks from legal:

1) Operational warranty: we can agree to a clause that says Redwood will not intentionally transfer customer content outside the regions contracted in the SOW except for: (a) short-lived telemetry and monitoring metadata needed for platform health (retention < 30 days, pseudonymized), (b) fallback routing in a declared outage (documented in the runbook). We propose language that references compliance with SCCs and UK IDTA + an obligation to notify and remediate.

2) SCCs / UK IDTA: we will accept addition of a UK Addendum and standard SCC incorporation. However, we cannot accept open-ended indemnities tied to downstream routing; suggest limiting to reasonable mitigation steps (notification, remedial routing, and documented rollback).

3) Subprocessors / KMS: Annex A will be provided. For subprocessors that hold encryption keys at rest (HSM/KMS) we can provide attestation of region and control owner, but not raw key material. If WellBridge requires HSM residency evidence we can provide KMS region mapping and SOC2 reports for the provider.

I've attached a suggested redline (high level) and a proposed TIA scope for Jordan's input. If procurement needs a DocuSign-ready DPA we can prepare that after redlines.

Next steps: Jordan, please confirm whether telemetry described above is indeed short-lived and whether we need to block any metrics from leaving EU/UK. Grace, I'll be available Monday for a 30-min sync to finalize language.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@wellbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational warranty & cross-border transfer checklist

Hi all — technical clarifications from infra/serving runtime perspective:

- Telemetry & metrics: platform metrics and aggregated telemetry are collected for health and are processed in control-plane services. We can scope the TIA so aggregated metrics (no PII) are pseudonymized and retained up to 21 days for alerting. We can configure region-bound metrics ingestion for WellBridge's tenant (EU-only ingestion endpoints) as part of Private/Dedicated setups; hosted customers receive region-aware routing by default but may have cross-region failover for continuity.

- KV cache and model context: KV caches are stored in regional caches tied to serving clusters. In severe failover we have a documented fallback where caches are rebuilt from model inputs; we do not replicate full application payloads outside region by default.

- Subprocessors that may see metadata outside region: monitoring (PagerDuty metrics sink), error-aggregator (Sentry-like), and long-term logging (archival) — we can provide jurisdiction mapping in Annex A. For keys: our customer-managed KMS option keeps keys in the customer's region; for hosted KMS we use cloud provider KMS with region-mapped keys and can provide attestation of region and key policy.

Action items I recommend in TIA: list endpoints that accept EU-only ingestion, document fallback triggers (latency/region outage thresholds), and describe cache rebuild behavior. I can produce a short appendix for the DPA describing these operational triggers.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
